investigationFindings.clientGap: src/lib/teamClient.ts had fetchTeamRoster (read) and pure seat-arithmetic helpers (seatCounts, canInvite, canActOn, isLastOwner) but no function that POSTs anything. Confirmed by reading the full file (202 lines) before writing any code.
investigationFindings.serverContractAsClaimedByDispatch: POST api/property-explorer/v1/team/invitations, body {email, role}, 201 on success, 400 with error in {invalid_email, invalid_role}. This was NOT independently re-derived from server source -- legacy-design-tools is not cloned into this working clone -- so the code and this checkpoint both mark it as dispatch-asserted, not independently verified.
investigationFindings.allowlistGapFound: api/_lib/deep-allowlist.ts's P-94 comment on the existing 'api/property-explorer/v1/team/members' GET entry read literally: 'Writes stay off until the client has a write path; invite UI is display-only.' This is the second, independent confirmation (beyond the dispatch's own framing) that the write path was deliberately withheld, not merely unbuilt by omission -- and it is the single most likely place a real client to have a POST fail invisibly: spine-deep.ts checks the session cookie BEFORE the allowlist, so a signed-out probe of a missing entry looks identical to a listed one (documented failure precedent in the same file for ai-connections and, once, the billing portal).
investigationFindings.settingsModalGate: SETTINGS_RUNNABLE explicitly excluded team_invite with an inline comment naming the exact same reason. runAction's switch had team_invite and unlock_expiring sharing one dead arm ('Unreachable: SETTINGS_RUNNABLE excludes both, with reasons').
investigationFindings.nextActionContextGate: lib/nextAction.ts's inviteTeammateRung only ever fires when context==="team" (nextAction(section, ...) is called with the live SettingsModal section), which means the rail can only ever propose team_invite while the Team tab -- and therefore the Invite panel -- is already on screen. This determined the CTA wiring: no cross-tab navigation is needed, only a focus signal into the already-rendered form.

adversarialReviewAtCP1: Risk: forgetting the allowlist entry ships a POST that 403s for every real signed-in user while looking fine in this client's own unit tests (which mock fetch and never touch spine-deep.ts). Mitigation: added the entry in the same change, plus a narrow allowlist test built from the client's own exported path constant rather than a second hand-typed literal, matching the exact pattern the file's BILLING_PORTAL_PATH / A-062 test already uses for this exact failure class.

Risk: fabricating the invitation's response shape (id, created-at, etc.) that the dispatch did not specify, which ENFORCEMENT.md's fail-closed discipline treats as inventing a resolution for a value that was not actually resolved. Mitigation: sendTeamInvite does not parse or expose anything from the 201 body beyond the bare 'sent' outcome; the UI treats the roster GET as the only source of truth for what the account now contains, refetching after a send rather than optimistically rendering a locally-constructed row.

Risk: a refused invite (unread seats / at capacity) still letting someone type into the field and hit submit, discarding the attempt silently. Mitigation: the email input and role toggle are disabled on the same inviteAllowed boolean the refusal copy already reads, not just the submit button.
